paper.title: BanditSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding via Bandit Algorithms

settings.name_in_paper: BanditSpec hyperparameter selection, stochastic case (stationary mean values)
unmapped: Rewards are not i.i.d.: only the conditional mean given the history and chosen arm is stationary (Assumption 4.1); rewards are martingale-type
Rewards (number of accepted tokens) lie in [1, L+1]; learner knows the maximum speculation length L
Objective is the stopping-time regret: difference in expected number of rounds until an EOS token appears, versus always playing the best arm; the horizon is a random stopping time
settings.definition_quote: There exist $K$ values $\{\mu_i\}_{i\in[K]}\subset [1,L+1]$, such that conditioned on the history $\calH_{t-1}$ and the chosen arm $I_t$ at time $t$, the expected number of the accepted tokens $\bbE[Y_{I_t,t}\mid \calH_{t-1},I_t] = \mu_{I_t}$.

settings.name_in_paper: BanditSpec stochastic case under greedy decoding (lower bound)
unmapped: Conditional distribution of accepted-token length given history and arm i equals a fixed P_{S_i} on {1,...,L+1} (Assumption D.2), with finite pairwise KL over the class of hyperparameter specifications
Greedy decoding; stopping-time regret; asymptotics as generation length len(pt_tau_c) -> infinity along a sequence of prompts
settings.definition_quote: Given any bandit configuration $\nu$ and initial prompt $\prompt$, conditional on the history $\calH_{t-1}$ and the selected arm $I_t$ at round $t$, the distribution of the length of the accepted tokens $\bbP(\;\cdot\mid \prompt,\calH_{t-1},I_t=i) = P_{S_i}(\,\cdot\,)$. For any two hyperparameter specifications $S,S^\prime \in\calS_{all}$, we have $\KL(P_S,P_{S^\prime})<\infty$.

settings.name_in_paper: BanditSpec hyperparameter selection, adversarial case (oblivious adversarial mean values, greedy decoding)
unmapped: Rewards (accepted-token lengths) lie in [1, L+1]; learner knows L
Stopping-time regret: E[ST(ALG)] - min_i ST(ALG_i), horizon is a random stopping time (EOS)
settings.definition_quote: Let the number of accepted tokens generated by hyperparameter $S_i$ at time step $t$ be $y_{i,t}=\len(X_{i,t})$. We assume $\{y_{i,t}\}_{i\in[K],t\in\bbN}$ is fixed by the environment before the algorithm starts.

symbols.L_spec: maximum speculation length L (rewards in [1, L+1])
symbols.N_len: expected length E[len(pt_{tau_c})] of the sequence generated by canonical decoding

conditions: Assumption 4.1 (stationary conditional mean of accepted-token length)

source.quote:
Under Assumptions~ef{ass:mean} and~ef{ass:finiteLen}, given any prompt $\prompt\in\calX^*$ and bandit configuration $
u$, the expected stopping time regret of Algorithm~ef{algo:SDbandit} with $\alg=\,$Algorithm~ef{alg:SpecDecUCB} ($\specucb$) is upper bounded as $\Reg(\alg,\prompt,
u) = O(mH(\prompt,
u)\cdot L^2 \log bE[\len(\prompt_{	au_{mc}})])$.

results.notes: Quantity is stopping-time regret (expected number of decoding rounds minus that of best fixed hyperparameter), mapped to 'other'. H(pt,nu)=sum_{i!=i*} 1/(mu_{i*} Delta_i). Proof gives explicit bound sum_i (Delta_i/mu*)(4 + 2L^2/Delta_i^2 (1+2 log(LK E[len]^2/(Delta_i delta)))) + pi^2 delta/6 + K.

symbols.kl_S_i: inf over S in the hyperparameter class of KL(P_{S_i}, P_S) subject to E_{P_S}[X] > mu_{i*} (K_inf-type quantity)
symbols.N_len: generation length len(pt^m_{tau_c}) (deterministic under greedy decoding)

conditions: sequence of prompts with len(pt^m_{tau_c}) -> infinity

symbols.p_star: truncated-geometric parameter p_{i*} of the optimal arm

conditions: all arms' accepted-length distributions are truncated geometric on [1, L+1] (TGD class)

source.label: prop:stoc_tightness
source.quote: Let $\calS_{\mathrm{TGD}}=\{S:P_S \mbox{ satisfies \eqref{equ:truncatedGeo}}\}$. Let $\{S_i\}_{i=1}^K\subset \calS_{\mathrm{TGD}}$ and $S_i$ satisfies~\eqref{equ:truncatedGeo} with $p_i$, then $\liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac{\Reg(\alg,\prompt^m,\nu)}{\log(\len(\prompt_{\tau_{\rmc}}^m))}\geq \rmH(\prompt,\nu) \cdot \frac{p_{i^*}(1-p_{i^*}^L)}{(1-p_{i^*})}$. Therefore, the upper and lower bound match up absolute constants and a $\frac{L^2(1-p_{i^*})}{p_{i^*}(1-p_{i^*}^L)}$ factor.

results.notes: Specialisation of r2 to truncated geometric distributions; for p_{i*} in (2^{-1/L},1) the proof gives sum (L/2)/(mu* Delta_i).

bound.expression_latex: 2L\cdot \min\bigg\{\sqrt{\len(\prompt_{\tau_\rmc}) K\log K}, 2L K\log K + \sqrt{\min_{i\in[K]}\ST(\alg_i) K\log K} \bigg\}

symbols.N_len: generation length len(pt_{tau_c}) (deterministic under greedy decoding)
symbols.ST_star: min_i ST(ALG_i), stopping time of the best fixed hyperparameter

source.label: thm:adv_UpBd
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:finiteLen}, ~\ref{ass:adv_mean} and~\ref{ass:stop}, given any prompt $\prompt\in\calX^*$ and bandit configuration $\nu$, the expected stopping time regret of Algorithm~\ref{algo:SDbandit} with $\alg=\,$Algorithm~\ref{alg:SpecDecEXP3} (\specexp{}), $\Reg(\alg,\prompt,\nu) \le 2L\cdot \min\{\sqrt{\len(\prompt_{\tau_\rmc}) K\log K}, 2L K\log K + \sqrt{\min_{i\in[K]}\ST(\alg_i) K\log K} \}$.

results.notes: Stopping-time regret E[ST(ALG)] - min_i ST(ALG_i). First branch is worst-case, second instance-dependent. Remark D.1 states an analogous bound (with expectations) for sampling decoding without a formal proof; not recorded separately.
